title: The School Garden
description: Students turn an empty piece of land into a vegetable garden.
instructions: Read the text about a school garden, then choose the best answer (A, B, C or D) for each question.

paragraphs.text: Behind Riverside Primary School, there was an empty piece of land. It was full of stones, old bottles and tall grass. Nobody used it for many years. One day, a science teacher, Miss Patel, had an idea.

She asked her students to help her turn the land into a garden. First, they picked up all the rubbish and pulled out the grass. Parents gave them tools and seeds. Then the children planted tomatoes, beans, carrots and sunflowers.

Every class took turns to look after the garden. They watered the plants every afternoon when it did not rain. The children also learned how plants grow and why bees are important. Some students who did not like science began to enjoy it.

In September, the children picked their vegetables. The school cook used them to make soup and salad for lunch. The sunflowers grew taller than the teachers! Now the garden is the favourite place in the whole school.

The garden also brought the school and the town together. Every Saturday morning, some parents and grandparents came to help. An old farmer, Mr Hughes, showed the children how to make compost from fruit and vegetable waste. The children were surprised that old banana skins and egg shells could help plants grow. Mr Hughes also built a small wooden house for the birds, and the children painted it blue and yellow.

In October, the school had a small market at the gate. The children sold extra vegetables, sunflower seeds and jars of tomato sauce to parents and neighbours. They made more than three hundred pounds. With the money, they bought a small greenhouse, so they could grow vegetables in winter too. Now there are always fresh salads for lunch, even when it is cold and dark outside.

Miss Patel is very proud of her students, and the head teacher is happy too. Last spring, a newspaper wrote about the garden, and two other schools in the town visited it to learn. Now those schools want to start gardens of their own. 'It all started with an empty piece of land and an idea,' Miss Patel says. 'Children can do amazing things when we give them a chance.'
